text: The department shall deposit 10% of the total gross revenue from sales of liquor with the state treasurer to be credited to the Uniform School Fund and used to support the school lunch program
note: Text read from the pinned enrolled bill.

text: 10% of the total gross revenue from sales of liquor (subsection unchanged by 2012 H.B. 354; still the existing text that 2020 H.B. 16 amended)
evidence: 2012 H.B. 354 enrolled (effective 2012-07-01) and 2020 H.B. 16 enrolled, both read online
note: Versions in force between 2012-07-01 and 2020 were not read one by one. 2012 H.B. 354 also routed the markup through the State Tax Commission into a Markup Holding Fund that paid this deposit (fund 5481; FY2013 transfer $14,998,002, zero balance after FY2014).

text: The department shall deposit 10% of the total gross revenue from sales of liquor with the state treasurer to be credited to the Uniform School Fund and used to support the school meals program

text: After the deposit made under Section 32B-2-304, the department shall deposit 1% of the total gross revenue from the sale of liquor with the state treasurer to be credited to the fund to be used by the Department of Public Safety
evidence: 2011 S.B. 314, enrolled (enacts 32B-2-305, Alcoholic Beverage Control Act Enforcement Fund, effective 2011-07-01), lines 1236-1238
note: DABS reports this deposit as 'Transfer to SBI' (the Department of Public Safety's State Bureau of Investigation).

text: After the deposit made under Section 32B-2-304 for the school lunch program, the department shall deposit 1% of the total gross revenue from the sale of liquor with the state treasurer to be credited to the fund
evidence: 2012 H.B. 354 enrolled (effective 2012-07-01), lines 160-163, and 2013 H.B. 399 enrolled (effective 2013-05-14), lines 366-369, read online; neither changes the 1% (2012 S.B. 4001, introduced version read, does not either)
note: The enactment inventory (metadata/legal_history/utah_enactments.csv) ends with the 2013 session, so an amendment taking effect late in FY2014 is not excluded. DABS's 'Transfer to SBI' is 1.000% of sales in FY2014.

text: 1% of the total gross revenue from the sale of liquor (the rate of the 2013 text)
evidence: Not read: the enactment inventory ends with the 2013 session, so later amendments of 32B-2-305 are not listed
note: Inferred from DABS's reported 'Transfer to SBI', which is 1.000% of sales in FY2015-FY2020.

text: 0.875% of the total gross revenue from the sale of liquor
